source: Chandler and Sweller (1992) The split-attention effect as a factor in the design of instruction
finding: Founding paper of the effect. Only the citation page was opened; the paper text was not reachable this session. Later reviews say it showed that diagrams plus separate text hurt learning when each source is unintelligible alone, and that integrating them helps.
numbers: Not read. Do not quote figures from this paper until the full text is opened.
limits: Experiment-level numbers (N, means, F) are missing. Cited second-hand via Sweller 1994 and Kalyuga 1999.
agent_relevance: Primary origin of the integrate-do-not-separate rule for prompts. Needs a full-text pass.

source: Kalyuga, Chandler, Sweller (1999) Managing split-attention and redundancy in multimedia instruction
finding: Defines split attention: several sources are hard or impossible to understand alone and must be mentally integrated. Learners hold text in working memory while searching the diagram for the matching part. Search and matching use memory that is then not available for schema learning.
numbers: Two computer-based experiments with trade apprentices; Exp 1 N=34, Exp 2 N=16.
quote: Search and matching related disparate information requires working memory resources that consequently are unavailable for schema acquisition
limits: Small samples. Apprentices, technical content (soldering, starter circuit).
agent_relevance: Gives the mechanism in prompt terms: if the model must find which rule matches which example, that search is spent effort. Put the label where it is used.

source: Kalyuga, Chandler, Sweller (1999) Managing split-attention and redundancy in multimedia instruction
finding: Exp 1: soldering fusion diagram. Audio text beat visual text (split attention), and audio text beat visual plus audio text (redundancy). Dual presentation of the same words was the worst format.
numbers: Visual+Audio n=12, Visual n=11, Audio n=11. Effectiveness ANOVA: fault-finding F(2,31)=7.74; multiple choice F(2,31)=10.66; Newman-Keuls: Audio better than both others.
quote: the dual-mode duplication format was the worst of the three instructional procedures
limits: Modality fix works only if the audio is short enough for memory. Means are shown only in figures, not text.
agent_relevance: Repeating the same content in two forms in one prompt can hurt, even when it looks safe.

source: Kalyuga, Chandler, Sweller (1999) Managing split-attention and redundancy in multimedia instruction
finding: Exp 2: colour-coding diagram parts and matching text parts cut the search. The colour group rated load slightly lower and scored higher on multiple choice than the conventional separate format.
numbers: N=16, 8 per group. Colour group took longer to study (n.s., F(1,13)=2.42). Load difference was only marginal; multiple-choice gain was significant after ANCOVA on study time.
limits: Authors warn that more than about five colours at once may add load and erase the gain.
agent_relevance: Cheap alternative to full integration: consistent tags or IDs that link a rule to the place it applies.

source: Kalyuga, Chandler, Sweller (1999) Managing split-attention and redundancy in multimedia instruction
finding: Boundary condition stated by the authors: integration is needed only if the sources are unintelligible alone. If a text just restates a self-contained diagram, integrating it adds load. This is the redundancy effect.
numbers: Claim in the introduction and discussion; backed by Exp 1 redundancy result.
limits: Intelligibility depends on the learner (see expertise reversal, a parallel subfield).
agent_relevance: Do not integrate or repeat what the model already gets from the main source. Drop restatements.

source: Kalyuga, Chandler, Sweller (1999) Managing split-attention and redundancy in multimedia instruction
finding: Load was measured by a single 7-point rating of how easy or hard the material was to understand, combined with test scores into an efficiency score E=(P-R)/sqrt(2) (Paas and van Merrienboer).
numbers: Rating 1 (extremely easy) to 7 (extremely difficult). Efficiency uses z-scores of performance P and load R.
limits: Subjective single-item ratings are the weak link of the whole line (see Beege 2019, Cierniak 2012).
agent_relevance: Shows how weak the load measurement is. For our agent, measure accuracy at equal tokens instead of imagined load.

source: Sweller (1994) Cognitive load theory, learning difficulty, and instructional design
finding: Sweller's own summary. Conventional geometry worked example: diagram tells nothing alone and solution steps are unintelligible alone, so the learner must integrate them. That effort is extraneous because it comes only from the format. Integrated formats were learned faster with higher test scores in many experiments.
numbers: Cites Tarmizi and Sweller 1988; Sweller et al. 1990; Chandler and Sweller 1991, 1992; Purnell, Solman, Sweller 1991; Ward and Sweller 1990. No pooled number given.
quote: an extraneous cognitive load is imposed
limits: Narrative review, no effect sizes. Materials were chosen by authors with high element interactivity.
agent_relevance: Clear definition to use when auditing prompts: what effort comes only from layout?

source: Sweller (1994) Cognitive load theory, learning difficulty, and instructional design
finding: Not all integration helps. Chandler and Sweller (1991) used a labelled heart-and-blood-flow diagram with text restating it. The diagram was self-explanatory, so the text was redundant, and integrating it forced students to process the text.
numbers: No figures given in this review.
limits: Described second-hand.
agent_relevance: Integrating a redundant block makes the model attend to it. Delete it instead.

source: Sweller (1994) Cognitive load theory, learning difficulty, and instructional design
finding: Element interactivity moderates the effect. Extraneous load hurts mostly when intrinsic load is already high. Sweller and Chandler (1994): split-attention and redundancy effects appeared for numerical control programming but not for word-processor commands.
numbers: Two content types; no figures in this review.
quote: a high extraneous cognitive load may be irrelevant because students are readily able to handle low element interactivity material
limits: Prediction that effects may vanish on low-interactivity material; a later meta-analysis found a small, non-significant effect there (see Beege 2019 citing Ginns).
agent_relevance: Prompt clean-up pays on hard multi-part tasks, not on easy ones. Test easy items separately (G12).

source: Sweller (1994) Cognitive load theory, learning difficulty, and instructional design
finding: Partially completed problems and worked examples are other ways to remove extraneous load; Sweller says the point is eliminating extraneous load, not replacing problems with examples.
numbers: Cites Paas 1992; van Merrienboer and de Croock 1992.
limits: Review only.
agent_relevance: Links to the worked-example subfield; keep out of this one.

source: Clearing House Unterricht (2019) Kurzreview 23 of Schroeder and Cenkci (2018) meta-analysis
finding: Summary of Schroeder and Cenkci (2018, Educational Psychology Review 30, 679-701). Integrated text and picture beat separated text and picture across 58 comparisons. Opened a German summary, not the meta-analysis itself.
numbers: Overall g=0.63 (medium), 58 effects. Earlier Ginns (2006) given here as g=0.72 on 37 effects.
limits: Second-hand. Mostly lab studies. Reviewers call the study selection description vague.
agent_relevance: Realistic size to expect for layout fixes: medium, not huge.

source: Clearing House Unterricht (2019) Kurzreview 23 of Schroeder and Cenkci (2018) meta-analysis
finding: Moderators from the 2018 meta-analysis. Largest effect on worksheets and for 2-D pictures and when text and picture add to each other. Static pictures beat animated or interactive ones. Duration of study and test type (recall versus transfer) did not matter significantly.
numbers: Worksheets g=0.80 (n=28 effects); computer-based g=0.50 (n=20); 2-D pictures g=0.71; complementary text and picture g=0.72; mobile device g=0.04 (n=1).
limits: Several cells have 1 to 7 effects. Mathematics/physics smaller effect. Table read from a PDF extraction, so column alignment is partly inferred.
agent_relevance: Effects are largest when the two sources are complementary and each needs the other, which is the case of a rule plus its case in a prompt.

source: Clearing House Unterricht (2019) Kurzreview 23 of Schroeder and Cenkci (2018) meta-analysis
finding: Discrepancy in effect size for the older Ginns meta-analysis. Clearing House gives g=0.72 (37 effects). Frontiers articles cite d=0.85 (95% CI 0.68-1.02) and one ACU summary d=0.89 for 50 studies (spatial plus temporal contiguity).
numbers: g=0.72 (37) vs d=0.85 vs d=0.89 (50 studies, mixes temporal contiguity).
limits: Original Ginns 2006 paper was not opened. Likely different subsets (spatial only vs both). Do not cite one number as the effect.
agent_relevance: Quote a range, 0.6 to 0.9, until the primary is read.

source: Beege et al. (2019) Spatial continuity effect vs. spatial contiguity failure
finding: Two experiments on text labels around a picture. In Exp 1 the separated format did NOT score lower than integrated formats on retention or transfer: the core split-attention contrast failed. A medium distance gave the best transfer.
numbers: Exp 1 N=98: separated vs integrated contrast retention t=0.66, p=.51; transfer t=1.47, p=.15. Quadratic medium-best contrast on transfer t=2.19, p=.03; retention n.s. (p=.93). Exp 2 N=85: quadratic contrast retention t=2.06, p=.04; transfer t=2.54, p=.01.
limits: Synapse and Stirling-engine materials, university students, load measured by a short questionnaire the authors call possibly inappropriate. Medium group reported lower intrinsic load too, which should not change.
agent_relevance: Closer is not always better. A label crammed into the item it describes may clash with nearby unrelated items. Keep related things adjacent but separated from unrelated ones.

source: Beege et al. (2019) Spatial continuity effect vs. spatial contiguity failure
finding: Names mixed evidence in the literature: Florax and Ploetzner (2010) mixed results; Schmidt-Weigand et al. (2010) could not replicate; Jarodzka et al. (2015) found benefits of low proximity. Notes that studies rarely report the actual distance in the integrated condition.
numbers: Reported as a pointer; the cited papers were not opened.
limits: Second-hand characterization by Beege et al.
agent_relevance: Boundary conditions are real. Run our own tests rather than trust a single rule.

source: Beege et al. (2019) Spatial continuity effect vs. spatial contiguity failure
finding: Two accounts of the effect are laid side by side. Cognitive load theory: separated sources add extraneous load through search and holding in working memory. Cognitive theory of multimedia learning: learner must map between verbal and pictorial models; adjacent unrelated items cause micro-switching (contiguity failure).
numbers: Cites Ginns (2006) moderator: high complexity d=0.78, low complexity d=0.28 (n.s.), as reported second-hand.
limits: Descriptive framing only; no formal model with parameters exists.
agent_relevance: Neither account is computational. For an LLM the nearest analogue is attention dilution; test it, do not assume it.

source: Cierniak (2012) dissertation, Tuebingen: facilitating and inhibiting learning by spatial contiguity (repository abstract)
finding: Load mediates only a small share of the effect. In Study 1 (kidney text and graphic), format did not change secondary-task performance, a direct load measure. Subjective extraneous load mediated 8% and 16% of the effect; subjective germane load mediated 9% and 18%.
numbers: Study 1 N=103 (secondary task in two thirds). Extraneous mediation 8% (labelling) and 16% (complex facts); germane 9% and 18%. Study 2 N=60 high vs low knowledge, germane load mediated 19% and 38% of the expertise reversal effect.
limits: Abstract page only; the full PDF download was truncated. Ratings subjective. Same group's 2009 paper is cited but not opened.
agent_relevance: Even for people, the less-extraneous-load story explains little of the gain. Do not build the agent around a load score.

source: Pouw, Rop, de Koning, Tabbers, Paas (2019) The cognitive basis for the split-attention effect
finding: Search-snippet summary only (PDF download was cut off). Three experiments varied distance between sources. Greater distance slowed text-picture integration but did not hurt a secondary task, and in realistic materials learning outcomes did not differ between conditions.
numbers: Not verified. Exp 1 pictures only; Exp 2 preregistered text-picture; Exp 3 realistic materials.
limits: Unopened. Needs full text before use.
agent_relevance: Possible failed-replication evidence that separation alone is not sufficient.

source: Schmidt-Weigand, Kohnert, Glowalla (2010) Explaining the modality and contiguity effects
finding: Cited by Beege 2019 as a study that could not replicate the split-attention effect. Not opened.
numbers: None read.
limits: Second-hand.
agent_relevance: Add to the failed-replication list.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large language models can be easily distracted by irrelevant context
finding: Adding one irrelevant sentence to grade-school math problems (GSM-IC) sharply cuts accuracy of code-davinci-002 and text-davinci-003 under chain-of-thought, least-to-most, program prompting. The model often uses the irrelevant number.
numbers: Fewer than 30% of base problems consistently solved after distractors; among baseline-solved problems no more than 18% consistently solved for all distractor types. About 4,000 problems (GSM-IC-4K) from 100 base problems.
limits: 2022-era GPT-3 family models. Added sentence sits right before the question.
agent_relevance: Direct LLM analogue of extraneous load from irrelevant text. Supports dropping irrelevant text from prompts.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large language models can be easily distracted by irrelevant context
finding: A cheap prompt fix helps: the instruction 'Feel free to ignore irrelevant information given in the questions' and distractor-containing exemplars both raise accuracy; the instruction alone with original exemplars matched or beat uninstructed prompts with distractor exemplars.
numbers: code-davinci-002 chain-of-thought micro accuracy 72.4 to 77.8 with instruction; least-to-most 77.5 to 80.6; the last table column (macro, inferred from extracted table) 8.3 to 20.0 for chain-of-thought. Self-consistency with 20 samples: correct answer present in 99.7% of problems.
limits: Table columns read from a PDF extraction, so which column is macro is inferred. No drop on original GSM8K from the instruction.
agent_relevance: Removing the text is stronger than telling the model to ignore it; but the instruction is a free fallback when text cannot be removed.

source: Liu et al. (2023) Lost in the middle: how language models use long contexts
finding: Position of the relevant passage matters. Accuracy is highest when the answer passage is first or last and falls when it is in the middle: a U-shaped curve. Query-aware placement did not fix multi-document QA.
numbers: GPT-3.5-Turbo accuracy can drop by more than 20% depending on position; at 20 and 30 documents the worst case is below closed-book 56.1%. Tested 10, 20, 30 documents.
limits: Older models; later long-context models may differ (Angle B to check).
agent_relevance: Put the decisive rule or item at the start or end of the prompt, not mid-list; prune distractor documents.

source: Levy, Jacoby, Goldberg (2024) Same task, more tokens
finding: Padding the same reasoning task with irrelevant text lowers accuracy even at lengths far below the context limit. Chain-of-thought did not rescue it for most models.
numbers: Average accuracy over tested models falls from 0.92 to 0.68 at 3000 tokens of input. Lengths about 250 to 3000 tokens.
limits: Synthetic task designed so all relevant spans must be used jointly.
agent_relevance: Length itself costs accuracy. Supports G11 and the drop-irrelevant-text rule.

source: Mirzadeh et al. (2025) GSM-Symbolic: limitations of mathematical reasoning in LLMs
finding: GSM-NoOp adds one clause that looks relevant but changes nothing. All tested models lost accuracy; weaker ones the most. Authors read this as pattern matching, not reasoning.
numbers: Drops up to 65% (Phi-3-mini over 65%); o1-preview also fell. Performance also declined as the number of clauses grew.
limits: Math word problems only; the no-real-reasoning reading is the authors' claim.
agent_relevance: Plausible-looking but irrelevant text is the worst kind of extraneous input. Filter it.

source: Sweller, Clark, Kirschner (2010) Mathematical ability relies on knowledge, too
finding: Short practitioner piece on worked examples and schema knowledge. Not specific to split attention.
numbers: None used.
limits: Low relevance to this subfield.
agent_relevance: Pointer to the worked-example subfield only.

source: Ayres and Sweller (2005) The split-attention principle in multimedia learning
finding: Handbook chapter on the principle; only the listing was seen. Defines the effect as occurring when learners must integrate several physically or temporally disparate sources, each essential to understanding.
numbers: None read.
limits: Paywalled.
agent_relevance: Standard definition to cite; read full text in angle B.

source: Cierniak, Scheiter, Gerjets (2009) Explaining the split-attention effect: is the reduction of extraneous cognitive load accompanied by an increase in germane cognitive load?
finding: Only the citation was seen. It is the key test of whether integration lowers extraneous load while raising germane load.
numbers: None read.
limits: Unopened.
agent_relevance: Follow up for load-mediation evidence.
